title.narrative: Share-Net Bangladesh

description.narrative: Share-Net Bangladesh is the country hub of Share-Net International, a Knowledge Platform focusing on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR). Share-Net Bangladesh is the first of Share-Net International’s country hub, drawing on the years of experiences and interventions by practitioners, researchers, and policymakers in the field of sexual reproductive health, especially placing SRHR at the centre of human rights. Share-Net Bangladesh aims to bring together the Communities of Practice (CoP) that consist of social and medical researchers, development practitioners, health workers, government officials and legal experts to engage with one another to find solutions and take critical issues forward. Share-Net Bangladesh is hosted by RedOrange Media and Communications. Priorities of Share-Net Bangladesh: * Promote interaction between the national, international, sustainable and empowered community of practice and encourage them to share learning. * To apply the knowledge to evidence-informed SRHR programs, policies and practices. * Enable the members and the strategic partners to connect, discuss, share, translate and jointly operate this knowledge network on SRHR. * Ensure the accessibility of the policymakers, practitioners and researchers to the knowledge platform and enable them to address the relevant knowledge gaps on SRHR scientifically, politically and practically

comment.narrative: Based on the SHIRIM III Evaluation, Share-Net Bangladesh (SNBD) stands out as a hub with affirmative outcomes and evidence-based approaches leading to positive policy impacts in the field of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR). SNBD's facilitated exchange during national learning sessions has enhanced policy influencing and practice within Bangladesh, highlighting the effectiveness of knowledge translation strategies. Comparatively, while other hubs like Burkina Faso and Colombia have also seen advocacy success and progress in practice change, challenges such as language barriers and concerns about potential exclusion have been encountered. However, SNBD's approach has provided a safe space for addressing SRHR issues and empowering members, indicating a robust institutionalization of knowledge translation efforts. Moreover, SNBD demonstrates significant capacity building, collaboration, and stable networks, similar to Jordan. In contrast, hubs like Burundi and Burkina Faso are on an evolving trajectory, focusing on making SRHR knowledge accessible and building reliable networks, indicating varied levels of institutionalization across hubs within the Share-Net network.

comment.narrative:
# Ms. Mushfiqua Zaman Satiar, Senior Policy Adviser- SRHR and Gender, SCS Partnership Coordinator and Youth Focal at the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands has been in good liaison with Share-Net Bangladesh. In 2023, Ms Mushfiqua was included in the Steering Committee in an advisory role in early 2022, she was present in 3 of the 4 steering committee meetings. She has been providing valuable insights on the SRHR situation in the country and based on her suggestion the 2023 activities were aligned. Ms Mushfiqua re-connected Share-Net Bangladesh team with different Dutch funded partnerships and Share-Net Bangladesh used these partnerships to align the annual activities in a coherent way so the impact of collective work is greater.
#Apart from this, Ms Mushfiqua has regular monthly meetings with Share-Net Bangladesh to guide the secretariat in a strategic way. 3 meetings took place from January 2023 till December 2023 with Ms Mushfiqua.
# Mr. Thijs Woudstra, Deputy Head of Mission, Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands joined as the Chief Guest of the grand Finale session at the 8th Annual Knowledge Fair 2023 and provided her valuable feedback at the Knowledge Fair on the knowledge Fair theme �SRHR and Education�. Ms Mushfiqua also joined the knowledge fair as a guest speaker.
#Dorine Thomissen, Ella De Voogs and Jannatul Munia joined a meeting at the Dutch Embassy to discuss the sustainability for Share-Net Bangladesh
